subject: Using external C++ code in Stan

messages.author: c02e0f9087e29020
messages.subject: Using external C++ code in Stan
parts:
Hi I have a follow-up question prompted by this discussion (Using external software inside Stan), but starting a new thread as some of the details are likely different. 

I had not previously seen the post 'Interfacing with External C++ Code', but what it describes might be very helpful for me. I use Rcpp to speed up the evaluation of large models. In earlier communication on Andrew's blog the message was that Stan couldn't interact with black-box models, and so to make things work the model would need to be programmed in Stan, to make use of the autodif. With the approach described in the recent post, is it now possible to pass stan a function written with Rcpp (ie C++), such that the autodiff could work with this function?   To be clear, this function would not provide gradient values (different to Ben B's problem).

Thanks - Nick

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using external C++ code in Stan
parts: With the approach described in the recent post, is it now possible to pass stan a function written with Rcpp (ie C++), such that the autodiff could work with this function?   To be clear, this function would not provide gradient values (different to Ben B's problem).

No — the key element Ben B’s question was that the black box
also supplied the gradients which would allow it to be integrated
into the autodiff library from the C++ side.

Remember that Stan programs are translated into C++ and then
compiled, so you already get decent optimization automatically.
